xrcvxx.text: Everything you need to know about Villager News, from how Villagers behave to the features that bring them to life.

entries.body: §i§7Villagers react to nearby mobs, blocks, player actions, trading, damage and plenty more. Try doing things around them and listen for a response.
§i§7Villagers are fully animated with custom movement, expressive voiceline animations and lip sync that brings their dialogue to life.
§i§7Choose between Vanilla, Actions & Stuff and Actions & Stuff: Flat Style Villagers in Settings to match the look of your world.
§i§7Villagers don't just react to you. They can interact with each other too, with conversations and unique exchanges between Villagers.
§i§7Reactions cover player actions, mobs, building, trading, Villager life, damage, world events, conversations and plenty more. Browse the Triggers & Reactions Guide to discover them all.

§i§7Villagers remember how you treat them. Trading and curing Villagers improve your reputation, while hurting or killing them lowers it. Villagers will even gossip about you with each other, changing how they react to you.
§i§7One of each special Villager News character spawns in your world. Explore different Villages to find them and trade for their unique items.
§i§7Wandering Traders have their own dialogue for trading, sold-out stock, successful deals and plenty more.
§i§7Baby Villagers have their own reactions and animations.
§i§7Rare Lines are longer, more unusual and over-the-top reactions. Use the Rare Villager Lines setting to disable them or make them more common.
§i§7Use Villager Chattiness in Settings to control how often Villagers speak, from completely silent to extremely chatty.
§i§7Enable Show Subtitles in Settings if you want spoken lines displayed on screen.

nlheqm.text: How triggers and reactions work, and why Villagers may not respond every time.

entries.body: §i§7Triggers are actions, events or situations Villagers can notice. Reactions are the dialogue and animations they may respond with.
§i§7Most reactions require a Villager to be nearby or able to see what is happening. Different triggers can have different detection requirements.
§i§7Reactions use cooldowns to keep dialogue feeling natural. Repeating the same or similar actions may not trigger another reaction immediately.
§i§7Not every trigger will cause a Villager to react every time. Cooldowns, distance, visibility, context and Chattiness can all affect whether a reaction plays.
§i§7Some reactions depend on additional conditions such as the Villager's profession, age, surroundings, your reputation or what is happening nearby.
§i§7Many triggers have multiple possible reactions, so Villagers won't always respond to the same situation in exactly the same way.
§i§7Villager Chattiness controls how frequently Villagers speak. Lower settings make reactions less frequent, while higher settings make Villagers more talkative.
§i§7Some reactions include longer and more unusual Rare Lines. Their frequency can be adjusted separately using Rare Villager Lines in Settings.
